# Pipeline streaming loses Store state and resets grid scroll

## Context

While validating the progressive-loading beat for #20185, the live DevIndex grid accepted a Username filter before its 50,000 records finished arriving, but a scroll returned to the top on later batches. The stream uses Neo 13.3.1. A controlled source-runtime probe at `7c8199fb1c` reproduces the same reset; the relevant Store, Pipeline, parser and Grid files are identical to current `origin/dev`.

## The Problem

Three controlled JSONL chunks through a normal Pipeline-backed Store and mounted Grid produce:

```text
second chunk: isStreaming unset, postChunkLoad=false → scrollTo(top, 0)
third chunk:  isStreaming unset, postChunkLoad=false → scrollTo(top, 0)
terminal:    postChunkLoad=true
```

The single-change diagnostic control `parser.store = store` makes both later notifications continuations and removes both reset dispatches. This control identifies the disconnect; it is not the proposed repair.

To reproduce, construct a Store with `pipeline.connection` returning a controlled `ReadableStream` and the real Stream parser configured with `initialChunkSize:1, chunkSize:1`. Bind a mounted Grid, enqueue three JSONL records separately, and observe Store load events plus `Neo.main.DomAccess.scrollTo`. No browser, external server or private data is required for this causal test.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: [the accepted #9186 correction](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/9186#issuecomment-3908525527) distinguishes first-load reset from intermediate and terminal streaming continuation. [#20056](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20056) separately preserves the reset default for ordinary mutations and excludes scroll anchoring.

- `Pipeline.beforeSetParser` supplies the parser's Pipeline, not a Store. Its Data Worker counterpart cannot hold the App Worker Store.
- `parser.Stream.read` still writes streaming state through `parser.store`; that reference is null in ordinary Pipeline use.
- `Store.onCollectionMutate` uses `isStreaming` for continuation. Store hydration and record-sort guards also consume it.
- `grid.Body.onStoreLoad` correctly resets an ordinary load; changing that consumer would hide the producer defect.
- `Pipeline.publishPipelineEvent` already forwards data/progress/error across the worker boundary. Store's active read already subscribes to those events and owns terminal settlement.
- `isLoadPending` is the separate reactive lifetime of any pending load. Its JSDoc must not be attributed to `isStreaming`.

Grace independently confirmed the disconnect and withdrew an App-only `parser.pipeline.store` repair after the Data Worker boundary check.

## The Fix

Restore progressive lifetime at the receiving Store's existing read boundary. Set streaming state when that read receives progressive data, preserve it through later batches, and release its ownership on every terminal path. Use per-read ownership so one settlement cannot clear another active stream.

Retire the parser's disconnected Store writes and its unused Store reference after checking callers; use the same read-owned fact for the terminal continuation notification. Keep the existing Pipeline event carrier. Place code and coverage in the existing data and grid files; no new subsystem or directory.

| Surface | Authority | Required behavior | Edge case | Docs / evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Store streaming state | existing hydration/sort guards and #9186 | true during progressive read delivery in either execution realm | cleanup on success, refusal, abort and destruction; overlapping reads retain their own ownership | Store JSDoc; controlled chunk/settlement tests |
| load.postChunkLoad | Store.onCollectionMutate and Grid.Body.onStoreLoad | later chunks and stream completion preserve the reader's position | first/new ordinary dataset behavior stays unchanged | existing load contract; actual Grid reset-dispatch witness |
| Pipeline data/progress path | Pipeline.publishPipelineEvent | retain the existing cross-worker data contract | no live Store reference crosses IPC | serialized App/Data receiver test |

Decision Record impact: none; this repairs an existing behavior using the existing transport.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: A red-first real Stream→Pipeline→Store test observes streaming state between chunks and continuation on later chunks; a bound mounted Grid issues no later-chunk top reset.
- [ ] AC-2: The same contract works through a Data Worker counterpart and the real serialized receiver path, with no App Store reference passed to the parser.
- [ ] AC-3: Success, empty input, rejection, abort and destruction clear owned state; settling one overlapping read cannot clear another active stream.
- [ ] AC-4: Ordinary replacement/reset, explicit append, filtering and sorting retain their existing contracts. No change to scroll anchoring or chunk sizes.
- [ ] AC-5: A focused browser witness on current Engine source preserves a scrolled grid through multiple arriving batches. Film footage remains separately subject to #20185's source/data and visual acceptance.

## Out of Scope

DevIndex data/blocklist policy; film publication; scroll anchoring for inserts above the reader; changing ordinary mutation reset defaults; new IPC operations or a general ingestion framework.

## Avoided Traps

A Grid-only no-reset patch leaves Store guards broken. Wiring `parser.store` or `parser.pipeline.store` repairs only a local parser. `isLoading` becomes false on the first batch, so it is not a stream-terminal witness. Source/runtime diagnosis does not certify released or deployed behavior.

**Intake accepted — prescription checked.** `src/data/Store.mjs` owns the receiving read, progressive admission and the guards that consume streaming state. `src/data/Pipeline.mjs#publishPipelineEvent` already crosses the App/Data boundary; the Grid consumes the intended notification and does not own the repair. Grace independently checked this responsibility and withdrew the parser→Store shortcut because it cannot cover the Data Worker path.

The current source-runtime falsifier uses the real Stream parser, Pipeline, Store and mounted Grid. Three separately delivered records yield two later-chunk top resets; the explicit parser-Store control yields zero. No tracked code is changed yet. Implementation will move state ownership to the existing Store read, retire the disconnected parser writes, and test cleanup/overlap plus both execution paths before the browser witness. The four existing Demo B PRs remain separate.

Same-session author intake: the creation chain is retained; independent prescription read is the prerequisite satisfied here. Existing Store loading and parser specs are the neighboring test homes. No new production module or directory is planned.
